question: A UX writer is unhappy that a Claude-drafted in-app error message describes the internal exception name and stack trace to end users. What is the most appropriate refinement for this audience?
options: A) Add a short apology sentence before the existing exception details in the message
B) Rewrite the message in plain terms describing what happened and what to do next
C) Keep the exception name but reformat the stack trace as a shorter numbered list
D) Move the stack trace into a pop-up that appears only when the user hovers over it
correct_answers: B) Rewrite the message in plain terms describing what happened and what to do next
explanations: Incorrect. Adding an apology does not address the underlying problem that the message still exposes internal exception details.
Correct. End users need a clear description of the problem and next steps in plain language; internal exception details are not meaningful to this audience and should be removed.
Incorrect. Reformatting the stack trace as a list still exposes internal implementation detail that is not useful to end users.
Incorrect. Hiding the stack trace behind a hover interaction still surfaces internal detail instead of replacing it with a plain-language message.
